claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The starting alloy demonstrates high strength and fatigue resistance.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by the formation and stability of a layered oxide scale.
The proposed scale consists of a protective, slow-growing Cr/Al-rich outer layer and a more reactive Ti- and Fe-rich underlying oxide layer.
Under oxidizing conditions, formation of the Cr/Al-rich layer limits further oxygen ingress.
Limiting oxygen ingress through the Cr/Al-rich layer preserves the integrity and mechanical performance of the fcc matrix.
Under reducing conditions, diminished oxidizing potential destabilizes the Cr/Al-rich oxide layer.
Loss or destabilization of the protective scale under reducing conditions permits oxygen or residual oxidants to penetrate the alloy.
Penetrating oxidants preferentially oxidize Ti-rich regions and produce degradation by internal oxidation.
A modest near-surface enrichment in Cr and Al can be introduced while retaining the bulk fcc phase and the intended composition constraints.
Near-surface Cr/Al enrichment will produce a more continuous and adherent protective oxide layer than the base alloy under oxidizing conditions.
The more continuous Cr/Al-rich scale will reduce overall oxidation kinetics and degradation relative to the base alloy.
Under reducing conditions, both the base alloy and the surface-enriched variant will exhibit increased internal Ti oxidation.
The original alloy forms a mixed oxide scale that is initially protective but degrades during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Degradation of the original alloy is especially pronounced in reducing atmospheres, where internal oxidation occurs in Ti-rich regions.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at approximately 600–800 °C in clearly oxidizing or reducing gas compositions.
Temperatures or exposure durations outside the proposed range may activate additional degradation modes.
Failure of Cr/Al enrichment to improve scale coherence or degradation resistance under oxidizing conditions would falsify the proposed governing role of the Cr/Al-rich layer.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says both alloys may show similar internal Ti oxidation under reducing conditions and does not define a directional difference between them, while the falsification rule treats absence of an expected difference in internal oxidation as falsifying. The expected difference is therefore not specified consistently enough to apply that part of the rule.
